image_description: A landscape photograph featuring three bison in a dry, grassy field. One bison is prominent in the foreground left, facing the camera with visible horns and head. Another bison is in the foreground right, grazing with its head down, showing its hump and hindquarters. A third bison is visible in the mid-ground background, walking laterally. The background consists of rolling hills and sparse vegetation under a bright sky.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The foreground left bison clearly displays a large, broad head with characteristic short, curved horns. The anatomy matches the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beard of long hair on chin and throat.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The foreground left bison shows a distinct beard of long, dark hair hanging from the chin and throat area.
The eye of the foreground left bison is visible and appears dark, consistent with the checkpoint.
Ears are not prominently sticking out; they appear small and partially obscured by the thick fur of the head, which is typical for bison.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Massive body with exceptionally tall, heavily built proportions at the withers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All visible bison exhibit the characteristic massive build and high shoulder hump (withers) typical of the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Shaggy dark brown fur covering forequarters forming prominent shoulder hump.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fur texture is visibly shaggy and dark brown, particularly dense around the shoulders and head, forming the iconic hump.
The bison in the foreground right shows a transition where the fur on the rear flank appears shorter and less shaggy compared to the forequarters.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short horns compared to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The horns on the foreground left bison are proportionally short relative to the massive size of the head and body.
The legs of all bison are obscured by the tall, dry grass. Hooves are completely invisible. Therefore, this checkpoint cannot be verified visually.
The tail of the mid-ground bison is visible and appears short with a darker, bushy end. The foreground right bison's tail is also partially visible and consistent.
